voyage.name: Cathedral
voyage.content: Huge 15th-century church on the site of the former great mosque; richly decorated with the central nave rising to 37 m. An ornate canopy and statue marks the final resting place of Christopher Columbus. If there's a queue for tickets then go to the nearby Church of Salvador (Iglesia del Salvador) and buy a combi ticket. Cathedral admission includes La Giralda, the minaret that is now the magnificent bell tower. Withi

voyage.name: Real Alcázar
voyage.content: A beautiful palace in Mudéjar (Moorish) style, built in the 12th century by the Almohad Caliphs. Greatly remodelled and extended in the 14th century by Pedro I the Cruel, its myriad rooms, extravagant architecture, lavish gardens including a maze, with many courtyards, ponds and secrets to be explored, make it a fascinating place to visit. The room where Christopher Columbus's journey across the Atlantic was planned

voyage.name: Hospital de los Venerables
voyage.content: A 17th-century retirement home and hospital for aged and sickly retired priests, restored by the Fundación to preserve an example of Andalusian architecture at its very best. Includes a resplendent Baroque chapel which is highly recommended, as well as the Santa Rufina painted by Diego Velázquez.

voyage.name: Torre del Oro
voyage.price: €3 adults, €1.50 seniors/students/children 6-14, free children under 6; €2 for audioguide
voyage.content: A 13th-century tower, the top of which is rumored to have once been covered in gold. It now houses the local maritime museum.

voyage.name: Alameda de Hercules
voyage.content: Authentic and less touristy plaza with local food opportunities.

voyage.name: Parque María Luisa
voyage.content: Built for the 1929 Iber-Americano World's Fair and now landscaped with attractive monuments and museums.

voyage.name: Palacio de Las Dueñas
voyage.price: Fee: €10 with audio guide, ask for reduced prices
voyage.content: Las Dueñas is a palace belonging to the House of Alba. It was built in the 15th century, with Renaissance architecture style and Gothic-Mudejar influences. The palace is one of the major historic homes in the city. The poet Antonio Machado was born here in 1875. It is also said that Amerigo Vespucci married in this chapel at the beginning of the 16th century. The Palace has a great collection of paintings (Ribera, Lu

voyage.name: Plaza de España
voyage.content: The site of the Spanish pavilion from the 1929 exhibition: the semi-circle has little ceramic maps of every region of Spain plus images of them and/or their history. It was also used in the filming of the Star Wars prequels. Visit it early in the morning on a weekday to see a long line of immigrants outside one of the government offices it now houses, or visit it right before it closes (officially at 22:00 but likely

voyage.name: Real Fábrica de Tabacos
voyage.hours: During term time only: Mon-Fri 10:00-20:00, Sat 10:00-14:00
voyage.content: The main building of the University of Seville was once the Tobacco Factory of Seville, and was constructed between 1728 and 1771 by Sebastián Van der Bocht. Over the main entrance, the triangular façade ends in a statue of La Fama (fame). The tobacco factory was then the largest industrial building in Spain. A monopoly assured high income, which is reflected in the factory's architecture and surrounding gardens. Its

voyage.name: Palacio de la Condesa de Lebrija
voyage.alt: Palace of the Countess of Lebrija
voyage.content: The palace is considered the 'best paved house-palace in Europe' owing to its collection of Roman mosaics and marble floors in the 'opus sectile' geometric style, which paved practically the whole of the ground floor. There is also a collection of well parapets, vases, amphora, columns and sculptures of incalculable worth. On the upper floor you can visit the residences previously inhabited by the Countess and her de

voyage.name: Casa de Pilatos
voyage.content: A 16th-century palace and generally thought to be one of the best in the city.

voyage.name: Palacio Arzobispal
voyage.content: It is in the historical section of the city and is home to various clergy and the Archbishop. On the outside you only can catch a glimpse of the patio but on the inside there are important works of art.

voyage.name: Archivo General de Indias
voyage.hours: Tue-Sat 09:30-17:00 (last entry: 16:30); Sun and public holidays 10:00-14:00 (last entry: 13:30); Mon closed
voyage.content: This Renaissance building houses extensive archives relating to the Spanish conquest of the Americas, and is designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Included in the collection are the diaries of Columbus. The archive hosts rotating special exhibits.

voyage.name: Metropol Parasol
voyage.content: An enormous wooden structure, designed by German architect Jürgen Mayer-Hermann, inspired by the Cathedral of Seville and in the form of giant mushrooms. Known to locals as 'las setas' (the mushrooms), the structure covers the Central Market and the Antiquarium; the top level contains a restaurant and provides some of the best views of Seville.

voyage.name: Museo de Bellas Artes
voyage.hours: 1 Sep – 31 Jul: Tue-Sat 09:00-21:00, Sun and holidays 09:00-15:00; 1-31 Aug: Tue-Sat 09:00-15:30
voyage.content: Considered by some as the second most important fine arts museum in Spain after the Prado in Madrid. The museum building is a former mercy convent renewed in the 17th century and the 15 exhibition rooms show a comprehensive picture of Sevillian art from the Gothic period to the early trends of the 20th century. The square just outside hosts an open-air art market on Sundays until around 13:30. Plenty of original pain

voyage.name: Museo Arqueológico de Sevilla
voyage.hours: 16 Sep – 31 May: Tue-Sat 10:00-20:30, Sun and holidays 10:00-17:00; 1 Jun – 15 Sep: Tue-Sat 09:00-15:30, Sun and holidays 10:00-17:00
voyage.content: It has one of the best collection of Roman-era artifacts in Spain, brought from nearby Italica.

voyage.name: Museo Antiquarium
voyage.content: A museum with excavated Roman and Moorish remains, discovered during construction of the Metropol Parasol. You can enter for free if you show your ticket for the alcazar, even if the ticket is a few days old.

voyage.name: Centro Andaluz de Arte Contempraneo
voyage.price: Visit monument €1.80; Temporary exhibitions €1.80; Complete Visit €3.01. Free on Tu-Fr 19:00-21:00 Sa 11:00-21:00
voyage.content: Contemporary art museum in the former Carthusian monastery of Santa Maria of Las Cuevas, which has a fascinating history as a clay mine, monastery, and ceramics factory. The site and expansive grounds are worth a visit in their own right, including a striking rose window, industrial chimneys, and orange orchards. This was one of the places where the remains of Christopher Columbus were buried, before ending up in the

voyage.name: Museo del Baile Flamenco
voyage.price: Museum: €10 adult, €8 senior, €6 child; performances: €20 adults, €14 senior, €12 child
voyage.content: Offers an experience for all the senses with ambiental music, videos, touch-screens and artifacts to be found in this 18th century building at the heart of the historical Barrio Santa Cruz. On Friday and Saturday evenings a spectacular show is hosted at a discounted price for visitors to the museum. Flamenco art and photography exhibitions are also on display and dance, singing, percussion and guitar lessons are offe

voyage.name: La Casa del Flamenco
voyage.content: A good spot to see real flamenco.

voyage.name: La Carbonería
voyage.content: Offers free flamenco shows nightly. Arrive early for good seats.

voyage.name: Semana Santa
voyage.content: The sombre Easter week processions feature thousands of people and go on all week, a spectacular display of conspicuous Catholicism.

voyage.name: Feria de Abril
voyage.content: Also known as "Feria de Sevilla" - a release after the somberness of Semana Santa. To say this is a huge party would be an understatement. Most if not all of Seville takes a week's holiday (the Wednesday of Feria week is a public holiday) and they plan for the fair months in advance. The fair is close to the river. It covers a huge area and contains hundreds of private and public casetas which are laid out to form st

voyage.name: Real Betis
voyage.content: Capacity 60,700. Their women's team play in Liga F (their top tier) at the nearby Luis del Sol training ground.

voyage.name: Sevilla FC
voyage.content: Capacity 42,500. Their women's team play in Liga F at Ramón Cisneros training ground 5 km southeast of the centre.

voyage.name: Plaza de Toros de la Real Maestranza
voyage.price: €7 adult, €4 senior or student, €3 child 7-11, free for child under 6; free on M 15:00-19:00
voyage.hours: Nov-Apr 09:30-19:00, May and Oct 09:30-20:00, Jun-Sep 09:30-23:00; on bull fighting days 09:30-15:00
voyage.content: Bullfighting is not a sport for all; those who are either squeamish or have convictions on animal welfare should stay clear, as the event concludes with the killing of the bulls. Failing that, a visit to the arena and the attached museum of bull-fighting is well worth the time. While it is not the largest, it is considered the most attractive bull arena in Spain due to its history.

voyage.name: Bodeguita Romero
voyage.content: A classic neighbourhood bodega, very popular with locals and serving excellent tapas.

voyage.name: El Librero Tapas y Quesos
voyage.address: Pasaje de Andreu 4, Barrio de Santa Cruz
voyage.content: Does cheese dishes, ham dishes, tapas, menu del dia, etc. Very popular with locals.

voyage.name: Los Coloniales
voyage.content: This tapas place is cozy and has only a few tables. Go there early to put your name on the board to get a table, then head inside for a couple of beers. Portions are large and food is very very good. Nice homemade desserts, too.

voyage.name: Duo Tapas
voyage.content: This bar offers a nice atmosphere and good food. The price is average and the size of the tapas is fair, but it may be crowded, so it's better not to go in a hurry, as you may need to wait for a table.

voyage.name: Naturalmente
voyage.content: Breakfast and lunch every day, with early dinner two nights a week - handy if you want to eat earlier than typical Spanish dining hours. The menu has a wide choice of breakfast "toasts", fruit and yoghurt bowls, cakes and pastries in the morning, changing to a range of lunch and dinner plates for lunch and dinner. There is a reasonable choice of vegan or vegetarian dishes, and overall the food is lighter than traditi

voyage.name: Cafe-Bar Las Teresas
voyage.content: A lively slice of ham heaven. Tourists and locals. If the sight of dead hogs hanging from the rafters offends you -- drink and eat elsewhere.

voyage.name: Restaurante Fez
voyage.content: Maroccan cuisine. Since you need a break from tapas. There are lots of other places serving Arabic food.

voyage.name: Habanita
voyage.content: In the centre of the city. Quiet open air restaurant with a very good selection of vegetarian and vegan foods.

voyage.name: El Rinconcillo
voyage.content: The oldest tavern around, try the Espinacas con Garbanzos (spinach with chickpeas) and Salmorejo, while watching the witty bartenders running around and writing your bill on the bar in front of you with, get this, chalk.

voyage.name: Parcería Café
voyage.content: Situated near Mercado Feria, Parcería is a tiny café serving coffee from a local roaster. Laptops aren’t allowed, but the coffee is worth a walk from the city centre.

voyage.name: Utopía Café
voyage.content: Hidden in a side street, Utopía is a takeaway-only café serving coffee from the same local roaster as Parcería.

voyage.name: Delatribu
voyage.content: A small takeaway café serving organic coffee and homemade pastry.

voyage.name: CafeTeaTe
voyage.address: Plaza del Altozano s/n Mercado de Triana, puesto 34-35
voyage.content: Located inside the Triana market, this café also serves breakfast sandwiches and other items. Their espresso shots are slightly longer than one might expect, but still decent. Make sure to ask about the current coffees when you order, they usually have one darker and one lighter roast.

voyage.name: B&B Naranjo
voyage.content: Budget hotel in old house near bus station, rooms are small with some on third floor, no elevator. Pleasant rooftop terrace. The a/c struggles in hot weather.

voyage.name: Oasis Backpackers' Hostel
voyage.content: Clean friendly hostel with rooftop pool. Daily activities such as walking tours, Spanish classes, bar games.

voyage.name: Oasis Backpackers' Palace Seville
voyage.content: Dorms in all sizes, lockers to put your backpack in and free linen. Roof-top terrace with chill-out bar to overlook Seville, guest kitchen, free breakfast and free internet/ wifi.

voyage.name: Sevilla Inn
voyage.content: Great location 100 m east of Giralda. Spacious terrace with views of the cathedral.

voyage.name: Triana Hostel
voyage.content: Clean well-run hostel, painted ceramic tiles, and green plants among cozy sofas. Nice roof terrace with hammocks. Rooms are average-small for a hostel with creaky iron bunk beds, safety boxes and short of space. Free breakfast and 3 (slow) computers with internet access. It's 3 blocks from the river in a nice neighbourhood with narrow streets and old houses.

voyage.name: Pension Vergara
voyage.address: Calle Ximenez de Enciso 11, Barrio de Santa Cruz
voyage.content: Simple pension but in a converted 15th-century convent.

voyage.name: Hotel Pasarela
voyage.content: Clean friendly place just behind the big plaza.

voyage.name: Hostal Callejón del Agua
voyage.content: Basic hotel, great location, very small rooms, street noise can be a problem.

voyage.name: Hotel Abanico
voyage.content: 22-room hotel in 18th century town house, small rooms but value for money, good location. Watch your step as you come out as traffic hurtles along the narrow street.

voyage.name: Hotel Abril
voyage.content: In a quiet street near Encarnacion Square 500 m north of centre. Small and simple hotel but clean, comfy and good value for money.

voyage.name: Hotel Bellavista Sevilla
voyage.content: Mid-range out-of-town hotel opposite hospital complex with 104 rooms with a/c. Has a café with outdoor terrace and à la carte restaurant, 24 hours reception, meeting rooms, pool and parking. Pets are allowed though some visitors have had problems over this.

voyage.name: Hotel Itaca
voyage.content: Small hotel north of centre, tiny rooms, several are blind. Mostly clean and comfy but they get a lot of street noise.

voyage.name: Hotel Las Casas de los Mercaderes
voyage.content: Comfy 3-star in great location 300 m north of Giralda. Some street noise, and don't bring a car to this pedestrianised area.

voyage.name: Hotel Monte Carmelo
voyage.content: Efficient modern hotel, 10 min walk to Plaza de España.

voyage.name: Hotel Monte Triana
voyage.address: Calle Clara de Jesús Montero, Triana
voyage.content: Simple hotel, clean and friendly, has parking.

voyage.name: Hotel Murillo
voyage.content: Small, clean friendly place in the Juderia. Small rooms and sometimes noisy but value for money.

voyage.name: NH Plaza de Armas
voyage.content: Efficient modern hotel on west side of city centre. Rooftop pool, Wi-Fi, meeting rooms and a restaurant.

voyage.name: NH Viapol Hotel
voyage.content: Modern hotel 1 km east of old city, airport bus and other transport stops just outside.

voyage.name: Hotel San Gil
voyage.content: 4-star going on 3, gets mixed reviews for comfort and service, 1 km north of city centre. Small rooftop pool and sun terrace.

voyage.name: Singular Apartments
voyage.content: Fully equipped apartments in 3 locations with large rooms and kitchens, also well suited for families or small groups.

voyage.name: Casa Romana
voyage.content: Comfy hotel 1 km north of city centre.

voyage.name: Eme Catedral Hotel
voyage.content: Comfy hotel in great location facing Giralda.

voyage.name: Gran Melia Colón
voyage.content: Plush hotel with spa, garage, restaurants and bars.

voyage.name: Hotel Alfonso XIII
voyage.content: Destination hotel, built for the Exposición in 1929, and converted into fabulous accommodation with prices to match. Has an outdoor pool, fitness centre, sauna and restaurant. Free Wi-Fi, public parking €22/day. Now part of Marriott.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa de la Palmera
voyage.content: In an affluent section of Seville just outside the centre city of the city. The hotel is a former private home of the Marquis and Marquise of Castilleja, built in the early 20th century and renovated for use as a hotel in 1999. Services and amenities include breakfast and room service, pool, gardens and a terrace, free parking and free Wi-Fi internet access.

voyage.name: Las Casas de la Judería
voyage.content: Upscale hotel next to a former synagogue. Splurge if you can on a suite, these are in the exquisite main building. Other rooms are in some three dozen nearby houses, pleasant enough but lacking the wowie-zowie factor.
